newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude market dead, four Brents kept.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude market dead, four Brents kept.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were dead on Friday with virtually nothing reported traded on the physical or cash markets as local traders turned their attention to other matters while their U.S. counterparts took a holiday.
A lone August Brent paper deal at $18.20 was the only crude contract to change hands all day, traders said.
August Brent slid further later in the day, closing 15 cents down on the IPE at $18.07 a barrel following through from Thursday's sharp losses.
Brent intermonth spreads and CFDs were also a shade weaker, with August/September talked at -16/-12 late in the day and CFDs for next week either side of August Brent evens.
"Everyone's been watching cricket or tennis or doing anything but trade oil," said one trader.
Buyers and sellers were at a stand-off on the physical market with little enthusiasm on either side.
With remaining July supplies thin, sellers were reluctant to drop offers, but buyers still complained of poor refining margins, despite the fall in outright levels.
"We need someone to make the first move (on North Sea crudes) but I'm not sure we'll see it today," said one trader earlier.
But despite an apparent lack of demand, four of the five Brent dates nominated loading dates on Friday were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline.
Stasco and Shell UK each kept one cargo loading July 19-21, Texaco was clocked with a cargo loading July 20-22, while Stasco and Statoil each kept one cargo loading July 21-23, traders said.
Poor margins were also deterring buyers of Russian Urals in the Mediterranean and depressing its value slightly despite a tight market for sour crudes.
A July 11-13 loader was traded on Thursday at dated Brent -69 cents, off the week's high of -65 cents.
